the effective mass of the 2D electrons in GaInAsP quantum wells is very close to the free-electron mass, and the carrier concentration in multiple quantum wells is very high, and the electrons are localized to the interfaces.

the electron concentration and effective mass of the 2DEG in n-type GaxlnxAsyPl-y-InP QW structures are dependent on the composition of the QW material, and that the 2DEGs in MQWs are confined to a single interface, forming a 'depleted' superlattice.
we have studied the properties of GaInASP-InP single- or multiple-quantum well structures, using the Shub-nikov-de Haas, cyclotron, and magnetophonon effect techniques.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the electronic properties of GaAs and InP based semiconductor quantum wells.
the study of the electronic properties of n-GaInAsP-In-P quantum well structures.
the study of the optical and electronic properties of semiconductor heterojunction structures.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the results obtained are in agreement with a simple model of a single two-dimensional electron gas at each heterojunction interface, with a depleted superlattice structure.
the GaInAsP/InP multiple quantum wells are not suitable for high speed, high power devices because the carrier concentration is low, the electron mobility is low and the carrier confinement is poor.
the results of the work described in this thesis are in excellent agreement with the predictions of the theory of the electronic properties of n-type GaInAsP and InP quantum-well structures.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we were able to measure the effective mass of the 2DEG, the density of the 2D carriers, and also the density of interface states.

the GaInAsP material is a very promising material system for high-speed, high-temperature electronic and opto-electronic devices, and that the GaInP-InP material system is a promising candidate for long wavelength infrared detectors.

we have been able to show that the effective mass in the quantum wells of GaInAs1-yP-y is smaller than that of the bulk material, that the two-dimensional carrier concentration is lower than the three-dimensional carrier concentration, that the carrier concentration is higher for the quantum wells of the multiple-quantums well structures, and that the carrier concentration in the quantum well structures is lower than the concentration of the bulk GaInAs1-xP-x material.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the properties of these structures are strongly dependent on the details of the growth and anneal processes.
the GaInAsP quantum well structures are excellent for the fabrication of infrared detectors.

the GaInAsP material system can provide the basis for a wide range of quantum structures with potential applications in opto-electronics, and that the Shubnikow-de Haas effect is a useful tool for characterizing such structures.
